premise: I gave my son and his wife $110,000 from my 403(b) to build an accessible in‑law suite onto their four‑bedroom house, securing a life‑estate agreement in writing; two years later they divorced and the daughter‑in‑law got the house in the settlement, then served me a 30‑day eviction notice saying the agreement didn’t bind her. I sued her and my son for joint unjust enrichment, won a $175,000 lien, and when the house went into foreclosure because they couldn’t refinance, I bought it at auction for the lien value — now I live upstairs and rent the in‑law suite to a widowed nurse, while both of them get a monthly bill for the property tax differential.
